title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of mobile accessibility, touch targets, screen readers, and responsive design.

questions.question: What is the recommended minimum touch target size in CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.5 AAA)?
questions.explanation: 44 by 44 CSS pixels ensures comfortable activation for most users.

questions.question: Inline text links inside a paragraph must always be at least 44x44 pixels.
questions.explanation: Inline links are exempt from the minimum target size requirement in WCAG 2.5.8.

questions.question: What is the primary navigation method for mobile screen readers like TalkBack and VoiceOver?
questions.explanation: Mobile screen readers use touch gestures: swipes, double‑taps, and explore‑by‑touch.

questions.question: How do you activate a focused element with VoiceOver or TalkBack?
questions.explanation: A double‑tap with one finger activates the currently focused element.

questions.question: On iOS, the VoiceOver feature that turns the screen black while running is called _____.
questions.explanation: Screen Curtain simulates blindness for sighted testers.

questions.question: Why must you provide a single‑pointer alternative for multi‑finger gestures like pinch‑to‑zoom?
options: Because multi‑finger gestures are not supported on Android
Because users with motor disabilities or screen readers may not be able to perform them
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.5.1 requires that multi‑point gestures have a single‑pointer alternative.

questions.question: What is the correct approach to avoid accidental activation on touchscreens (WCAG 2.5.2)?
options: Use `click` event (pointer up) or allow drag‑to‑cancel
questions.explanation: Actions should fire on pointer up or provide a cancellation mechanism.

questions.question: A website that forces users to rotate their device to landscape orientation fails WCAG unless landscape is essential.
questions.explanation: WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation requires support for both portrait and landscape unless essential.

questions.question: At what minimum viewport width should your content reflow without horizontal scrolling?
questions.explanation: 320 CSS pixels is the equivalent width at 400% zoom on a 1280px screen; WCAG 1.4.10 requires 320px.

questions.question: What is the safest way to ensure a responsive layout does not cause horizontal scrolling?
options: Use relative units and `max‑width: 100%` on all elements
questions.explanation: Relative units and maximum widths allow content to shrink and wrap naturally.

questions.question: Why should you avoid `role='application'` on mobile?
options: It takes over all screen reader gestures and can confuse users
questions.explanation: `role='application'` disables standard screen reader navigation gestures, which is disorienting on mobile.

questions.question: You can rely solely on the browser's device mode to test mobile accessibility.
questions.explanation: Real device testing is necessary for touch, gesture, and screen reader behaviour.

questions.question: What should you include to make a carousel accessible to keyboard users?
options: Arrow key handling and previous/next buttons
questions.explanation: Keyboard operability is required; provide arrow keys and visible controls.

questions.question: How can you test if your colour contrast is sufficient on mobile?
options: Assume it's fine if it passed on desktop
Use a mobile contrast checker app or the browser's DevTools
questions.explanation: Contrast tools work regardless of device; many mobile browsers support DevTools remote inspection.

questions.question: A user cannot complete a swipe‑to‑delete gesture. What is the appropriate remedy?
options: Tell them to use a different device
Provide a visible Delete button as an alternative
questions.explanation: Path‑based gestures require a single‑pointer alternative (WCAG 2.5.1).

questions.question: Mobile screen readers announce `aria‑live` regions regardless of where the user's focus is.
questions.explanation: On some mobile screen readers, live regions may not announce if focus is not on them; moving focus ensures announcement.

questions.question: Which HTML meta tag ensures proper viewport rendering on mobile?
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag instructs mobile browsers to use the device width as the viewport.

questions.question: Why is it important to avoid `display:none` on a `<label>` that's hidden for responsive design?
options: It makes the page load slower
It removes the label from the accessibility tree, breaking the input's accessible name
It's fine as long as there's an `aria-label`
questions.explanation: If the label is hidden with `display:none`, its association is lost. If you must hide it, use a `visually‑hidden` class or ensure an alternative name.

questions.question: A hamburger menu button should have which ARIA attributes when the menu is closed?
questions.explanation: `aria-expanded` indicates whether the controlled menu is visible.

questions.question: What is the best way to test for touch target size?
options: Use a ruler on the screen
Inspect the element's box model and ensure the interactive area is at least 44x44px
questions.explanation: DevTools box model shows the actual clickable area of an element.
